TESTED ON A LOCAL CPU · 2026.09.22

See words as you speak.
Refine before committing.

After comparing six open-weight speech models, v0.5.1 uses this pairing by default:
Zipformer for streaming drafts, SenseVoice for final correction.

Qwen and Fun made fewer Chinese errors on these samples, but took about 1.6 seconds to process a full clip. SenseVoice took about 0.18 seconds and improved both Chinese and English recognition: a useful balance for responsive dictation on this machine.

Correcting the final words

In one Chinese clip, the draft “盖甲等元素” became the correct “钙钾等元素” before submission. Three product-flow replays finished about 40–199 ms after stopping. This small sample excludes microphone and UI latency, retains trailing silence, and includes correction that may have started before stopping.

These results describe one machine and 60 public read-speech clips, not every accent, noisy room or personal dictation. Refinement does not improve the live draft itself. Failures fall back to streaming recognition; text already committed is never rewritten.
